This job is a great opportunity.

to take something that is not yours
past of 'catch': to find someone doing something
to agree that something bad is true
vocabulary.example: He admitted that he was wrong.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to feel sorry about something you did
to say what is wrong with someone or something
vocabulary.example: My father criticised my messy room.
She passed on her first attempt.

the loud noise after lightning in a storm
words that show you admire someone

fine_lines.title: have a go vs have a go at someone
fine_lines.explanation_ar: have a go (at something) = يجرّب أو يحاول: Have a go at this puzzle. أما have a go at someone (بعدها شخص) = ينتقده أو يوبّخه بغضب.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Have a go (at something)' means try: Have a go at this puzzle. 'Have a go at someone' (followed by a person) means criticise them angrily.

examples.sentence: I've never made bread, but I'll have a go.
The coach had a go at us for being late.

fine_lines.title: kiss something goodbye vs call it a day
fine_lines.explanation_ar: kiss something goodbye = تقبل أنك ستخسر شيئاً أو فرصة. call it a day = تقرّر التوقف عن العمل لبقية اليوم (أو نهائياً).
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Kiss something goodbye' = accept that you will lose something or a chance. 'Call it a day' = decide to stop working for now (or for good).

examples.sentence: If you miss the deadline, you can kiss the prize goodbye.
We've worked for eight hours – let's call it a day.

fine_lines.title: steal someone's thunder vs eat your words
fine_lines.explanation_ar: steal someone's thunder = تأخذ الانتباه أو المديح الذي كان لشخص آخر. eat your words = تعترف بأن ما قلته كان خطأً.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Steal someone's thunder' = take attention or praise away from another person. 'Eat your words' = admit that what you said was wrong.

examples.sentence: She stole my thunder by sharing my news first.
You said I'd fail – now you'll have to eat your words!

expressions.meaning_ar: يتقبّل خسارة شيء أو ضياع فرصة
expressions.meaning_en: to accept that you have lost something or a chance
expressions.example: The rain started, so we kissed our picnic goodbye.

expressions.meaning_ar: يُضبط متلبّساً أثناء فعل شيء خاطئ
expressions.meaning_en: to be caught while doing something wrong
expressions.example: My brother was caught red-handed eating my chocolate.

expressions.meaning_en: to decide to stop what you are doing for now
expressions.example: I'm tired. Let's call it a day and finish tomorrow.

expressions.meaning_ar: يعترف بأن ما قاله كان خطأً
expressions.meaning_en: to admit that something you said was wrong
expressions.example: He said our team would lose, but he had to eat his words.
Why do you always have a go at me?
Can I have a go at riding your bike?

expressions.meaning_ar: خذ ما شئت؛ استفد إلى أقصى حد
expressions.meaning_en: take as much as you want; make the most of a situation
expressions.example: There's lots of food left – fill your boots!

expressions.meaning_ar: يسرق الأضواء أو المديح من شخص آخر
expressions.meaning_en: to take attention or praise away from someone else
expressions.example: I was going to announce the plan, but Ali stole my thunder.

expressions.meaning_ar: يمرّ بخطوات صعبة كثيرة (وأحياناً غير ضرورية) للحصول على شيء
expressions.meaning_en: to do many difficult, often unnecessary things to get something
expressions.example: We had to jump through hoops to get a refund.

grammar.title: Passive with 'get' and 'be': caught red-handed
grammar.explanation_ar: نقول be caught أو get caught (مبني للمجهول) عندما يُكتشف الشخص: He was caught red-handed. She got caught cheating. التركيب: be/get + التصريف الثالث للفعل (caught).
grammar.explanation_en: We use 'be caught' or 'get caught' (passive) when someone is discovered doing something: He was caught red-handed. She got caught cheating. Pattern: be/get + past participle.
examples: The thief was caught by the police.

questions.question: 'Let's call it a day.' What does it mean?
questions.explanation_ar: call it a day = نتوقف عن العمل اليوم.
questions.explanation_en: 'Call it a day' means stop for today.

questions.question: The thief was ___ taking money from the till.
questions.explanation_en: 'Caught red-handed' means caught doing something wrong.

questions.question: 'I'll have a go at fixing it.' The speaker will...
questions.explanation_ar: have a go at + شيء = يحاول.
questions.explanation_en: 'Have a go at' + thing means try.

questions.question: 'My manager had a go at me.' The manager...
questions.explanation_ar: have a go at + شخص = ينتقده بغضب.
questions.explanation_en: 'Have a go at' + person means criticise angrily.

questions.question: You said I couldn't cook, but this cake is perfect. Now you must ___.
questions.explanation_en: 'Eat your words' means admit you were wrong.

questions.question: It was my big day, but my cousin announced his news first and ___.
questions.explanation_en: 'Steal someone's thunder' means take attention from someone.

questions.question: To get a visa, we had to fill in many forms and visit many offices. We had to ___.
questions.explanation_ar: jump through hoops = يمرّ بخطوات صعبة كثيرة.
questions.explanation_en: 'Jump through hoops' means do many difficult steps.

questions.question: 'Free fruit for everyone – fill your boots!' This means...
choices: Take as much as you want.
questions.explanation_ar: fill your boots = خذ ما شئت.
questions.explanation_en: 'Fill your boots' means take as much as you want.

questions.question: If you lose the receipt, you can ___ your refund ___.
questions.explanation_en: 'Kiss something goodbye' means accept you've lost it.
